newsitem.title: UK: Sugar freight business routine, new orders cited.
newsitem.headline: Sugar freight business routine, new orders cited.

text.p: Business was fairly routine on the sugar freight market on Monday, with interest noted for Far East origins and movement seen around the Middle East buying region, shipbrokers said.
Of the day's firmer business, E D & F Man was said to have fixed 14,700 tonnes of bagged sugar from Immingham to Tunisia for early April.
Man was also said to be on subjects with 19/20,000 tonnes in bulk from Puerto Quetzal to Casablanca/Black Sea for 8/15 April.
Cargill was also reported to be on subjects with 11/12,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Rio Haina to US Gulf/Atlantic for early April but further details have yet to emerge.
Cargill also quoted for 12/14,200 tonnes of bulk/bagged sugar from Thailand to Indonesia for prompt onwards dates.

Louis Dreyfus quoted for 25,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from 31 March/4 April and also amended its order from last week for a prompt 25,000 tonnes from the Philippines to the US east coast, now specifying west coast.

Shipbrokers said Glencore was open for 13,000 tonnes in bags from east coast Mexico to east Africa for 1/15 April and C.Czarnikow for 16,800 tonnes in bulk from Laemchabang or Sriracha to south Korea for mid-April.
Seven Seas quoted for 3,600 tonnes of bagged sugar from Port Sudan to Aden for prompt onwards dates, after last week's bagged order for 2,600 tonnes from the same destination to Aqaba.
Seven Seas was also in the market for 5/7,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Djibouti to Somalia for prompt onwards shipment dates.

Secretan issued an account order for 10,800 tonnes of bagged sugar from south China to Pakistan/Red Sea for 28 March/early April. It also quoted for 26/30,000 tonnes in bulk from Cuba to Iran for 1/15 April but shipbrokers said this could be an amendment of last week's inquiry.
David Bruce quoted two account orders for bagged sugar, for 3,000 tonnes to go from Guatemala to Peru for 24/28 March and 1,000 tonnes from Odessa to Poti for 27/31 March.
Shipbrokers said Czarnikow Rionda was still open with its three recent bagged inquiries.
Lastly, D.K. Shipping amended last week's account order for 12,500/15,000 tonnes of sugar in 50 kg bags from Topolobampo to Dubai for 17/22 April, adding Dubai as an optional destination.

In other news, the U.N. is said to have approved the sale of French sugar to Iraq worth some $18 million under the oil-for-food pact, with the contract involving the sale of 50,000 tonnes of French sugar.
The total amount of sugar purchased by Iraq from international firms under a December tender remains unclear, though some traders have estimated it at up to 150,000 tonnes.
The leader of Mexico's main sugar workers' union predicted that the national 1996/97 cane harvest would produce a record crop of 4.5 million tonnes of sugar.

At least 20 percent of Australia's 1997/98 cane crop is reported to have been hit by cyclone Justin during the weekend, with cane flattened across widespread areas of the main growing district of northeast Queensland.
